Andoni Iraola's Reds were rampant on Sunday as they took 10-man Manchester United to pieces with a 4-0 win at Anfield . Szoboszlai started the rout, hammering home the free-kick from the edge of the area that resulted from Leny Yoro's clumsy red-card challenge on Alexander Isak. top.title: Is Gent’s title challenge already begining to falter?
top.description: Is Gent’s title challenge already begining to falter? Rik De Mil will certainly not have enjoyed watching his Gent side this past weekend. Away to Beveren , the side lost 1-0 despite having a man advantage for the majority of the second-half. Arno Verscheuren was shown a red card just 10 minutes into the second half, but the Buffaloes were unable to make their superior numbers count. Instead, Gent saw Jearl Margaritha score the only goal of the game to help managerless Beveren to their first league win since the 12th of September. Gent, on the other hand, have won just two games in their last five in all competitions and are starting to see their title challenge falter somewhat. De Mil and his Gent side had started the season in fantastic form, and it probably shouldn’t be panic stations just yet. The defeat to Beveren was only their second of the league season, with the gap to Union St Gilloise now four points. That could become just one should Gent beat Union this coming weekend. However, the side have suffered from injuries to key players, including the former Union fan favourite Christian Burgess. While De Mil is known for playing attractive attacking football, it has been the defence that has shone for Gent this season, with just seven goals conceded in 12 games, the best defence alongside league leaders Union. After a European clash with FK Crvena Zvezda on Thursday, Gent will hope to get things back on track with a win over Union this weekend. With no play-offs and halving of points this season, if Gent have any aspirations of challenging for the league title they can ill afford to let the likes of Club Brugge or Union open up a decent lead on them this season, given how consistent both sides have been over the past few years. top.title: 49ers’ Nick Bosa bombarded by vulgar Spanish chants after shading Mexican fans
top.description: The fans in Mexico City were not ready to forgive Nick Bosa for comments made ahead of the San Francisco 49ers ‘ Sunday night showdown against the Minnesota Vikings at Estadio Azteca. Leading up to the game, Bosa made comments in the media that seemed to shade Mexican fans , going so far as to remark on their “soccer cheering” and saying, “some information given to the fans” so they know the appropriate time to cheer. Well, Mexican fans are going to cheer whenever they want, or they will heckle you. For Bosa, it was the latter on Sunday night. Bosa was booed mercilessly when he took the field at Estadio Azteca, but that was only the beginning. Throughout the night, Bosa was often met with chants of “culero” every time he was shown or involved in a play. top.title: 2027: We’re not jittery, opposition not ready – Bwala
top.description: Sekinat Osundiji Presidential spokesman Daniel Bwala has said the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) is not worried about the opposition ahead of the 2027 general election, insisting that its political rivals are not prepared for the contest. Bwala, Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Policy Communication, stated this during an interview on Channels Television, where he dismissed suggestions that the ruling party was apprehensive about the growing activities of opposition parties. He said the APC was confident about its political standing, adding that the opposition was not ready for the election. “I do not think the opposition is ready. Those who understand the political trajectory can see that they are already facing defeat,” Bwala said. His comments followed questions about President Tinubu’s decision to expand his campaign itinerary beyond the initial 12 states, amid reports of attacks on campaign materials and the president’s convoy. Defending the adjustment, Bwala described it as a strategic decision rather than an indication that the APC was worried about its political opponents. “President Tinubu is not scared. It is a matter of strategy. He is a chess player, who studies the moves of his opponents before deciding on his next move,” he said. He, however, acknowledged that the ruling party was working to secure voters’ support, saying it would be wrong to assume that Nigerians had already decided to re-elect the president. “We are not worried, but we are working hard because we respect the will of the people. We cannot take their votes for granted,” Bwala said. On the political situation in the North, Bwala described the region as a major battleground in the 2027 election, noting that the president’s campaign activities there were part of a deliberate strategy. He rejected suggestions that the North was united against Tinubu, arguing that the position of individual political leaders should not be interpreted as the collective position of the region. “There is no unanimous adoption of a candidate by any bloc in Nigeria, not even in the North. The position of one political leader should not be taken as the position of the entire region,” he said. Bwala also argued that the president had made significant efforts in the South-West, which informed his decision to concentrate more campaign activities in other regions. Addressing Peter Obi’s performance in the 2023 presidential election, the presidential spokesman said the Labour Party candidate benefited from religious sentiments surrounding the APC’s Muslim-Muslim presidential ticket. “Politics is about strategy. In 2023, Peter Obi benefited from the reaction of some Christians to the APC’s Muslim-Muslim ticket. That was one of the factors that shaped the election,” Bwala said. He further claimed that Obi had visited 12 major churches during the previous election cycle but had not maintained the same pattern ahead of 2027. top.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The camp of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has alleged a plot by some political actors to link him with the Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) in a campaign it claims is aimed at weakening his growing support in Northern Nigeria. The Peter Obi Media Office (POMR) raised the alarm on Monday, alleging that individuals within the ruling party and some opposition elements were coordinating a propaganda campaign to portray the former Anambra State governor as sympathetic to Biafran separatism. In a statement signed by its spokesperson, Idris Zekeri, the media office said the alleged campaign was intended to discourage Northern Nigerians, particularly young people, from supporting the Obi-Kwankwaso political movement. It alleged that the campaign could involve sponsored reports in Northern newspapers, interviews on radio stations in the region and coordinated narratives on social media. The media office also cited a claim by a social media personality, Gucci Commando, who allegedly said he had visited IPOB leader, Nnamdi Kanu, in Sokoto and attributed political endorsements in support of Obi to him. However, POMR described the claim as questionable, insisting that allegations of such magnitude required independent verification and should not be presented as established facts. The statement read in part: “The Peter Obi Media Office has expressed grave concern about credible intelligence indicating that certain actors within the ruling party, together with elements of the opposition, have hatched a coordinated anti-Obi propaganda effort aimed at exploiting Nigeria’s delicate ethnic and security divisions. “The alleged purpose of this effort is to falsely link Peter Obi to Biafran separatism and depict him as politically aligned with IPOB leader Nnamdi Kanu, apparently to distance Northern Nigerians, especially young people, from the Obi-Kwankwaso political movement.” The media office maintained that Obi was neither an ethnic nor a religious candidate, describing him as a Nigerian whose political vision and aspirations extended beyond ethnic, religious and regional divisions. It said his political objective was to address the country’s economic, security and governance challenges and build a nation that served the interests of all Nigerians. Zekeri said Obi’s commitment to justice, dialogue, national reconciliation and the rule of law should not be misrepresented as support for separatism. top.title: Differing account of ‘gentleman’s agreement’ between Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala as plot thickens
top.description: (Photo by Harry Langer/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images The latest reporting from Sky Germany’s Florian Plettenberg (via @iMiaSanMia ) adds another layer to the increasingly complicated discussion surrounding Jamal Musiala’s contract at Bayern Munich, particula rly when compared with the earlier report that Bayern believes a “gentleman’s agreement” with Musiala’s camp has been violated. According to Plettenberg, Uli Hoeneß met with Musiala’s agency at Tegernsee in August 2026. The meeting took place before Musiala’s condition was publicly disclosed and before his two collapses during the friendly matches against Leipzig and Heidenheim. Hoeneß was reportedly informed of Musiala’s health condition at the time, and the meeting was described as having taken place in a positive, trusting atmosphere. However, the crucial detail is what reportedly did not happen: no specific agre ements were reached regarding a potential contract adjustment if Musiala’s performan ces declined, and no assurances were made, either verbally or in writing. This new information appears to complicate the narrative outlined in the Süddeutsche Zeitung report that prompted our earlier coverage. That report claimed two legally non-binding gentlemen’s agreements were reached during a summer meeting between Hoeneß and Musiala’s agent, Christian Schmid — Bayern Munich would support Musiala through his recovery, and the contract could be adjusted in Bayern’s favor if Musiala continued to struggle with his health and medication side effects. The distinction between the two accounts is significant. The earlier report suggested an understanding existed regarding a possible contr actual adjustment if Musiala could not return to his previous level. Plettenberg’s reporting, however, expli citly denies that any such agreement, assurance, or commitment was made. That does not necessarily mean the two reports are entirely incomp atible. There could have been discussions about Musiala’s health, expectations, and the club’s concerns without eithe r party reaching a concrete understanding about modifying the contract. Even so, the latest reporting directly challenges the idea that Musiala’s camp agreed to a specific contingency involving his salary. Like every other aspect of this saga, we know some things, but not enough. For now, Bayern Munich’s frustration may be real, but the precise nature of any alleged gentleman’s agreement remains disputed—and that distinction matters enormously in this increasingly contentious saga. (Photo by James Black/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Just keep winning. It sounds overly simplistic, like there should be a deeper strategy behind what it takes to separate yourself in the Big Ten standings, and how you stack up against the national competition. But it’s been Kirk Ferentz’s mantra for decades now, and especially as of late during his weekly pressers. And I am willing to bet it was what was on the player’s minds when they took the field for the second half on Saturday versus Illinois. Saturday was the fifth time this season that Iowa has not allowed their opponent to score a single point in the second half. And on what looked to be a relatively quiet weekend for B1G matchups, chaos erupted. Undefeated UCLA lost at Michigan, Indiana lost at Washington, OSU was upset at Nebraska, and even Rutgers won at Penn State. Let’s take pause and look at the B1G conference standings. UCLA is on top at 7-1. Indiana, Oregon, and Iowa are now tied at 6-2 for second place. With Wisconsin, USC, and Ohio State all tied for third place at 5-3. Four more teams are tied for fourth place at 4-4. Fourteen teams in the Big Ten are now bowl eligible. So how is Iowa different this year? This game against Illinois was a microcosm of what this season has held. The Variety of Receivers Catching Passes Six different players had receptions on Saturday, and that’s actually on the low end for this season. More commonly, it’s seven or eight different players. And on Saturday, the top two receivers, in terms of total catches and yardage, were wide receivers Tony Diaz annd Reece Vander Zee versus tight ends. While we’re on the topic, I will call out that it is good to see tight end Thomas Meyer getting involved and making catches as the season progresses, as Iowa will need him next year after Addison Ostrenga and Zach Ortwerth graduate. The Variety of Play Calls & Weapons No longer is Iowa predictable, and the variety of players able to make a reception or rush for an end around sweep keeps defenses guessing when players like Diaz, Reece Vander Zee, or DJ Vonnahme go in motion. Now the wrinkle of Hank Brown getting the call for designed quarterback runs adds to the unpredictability. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images Welcome back to our look around the Brewers’ roster at potential targets that could help the team! As detailed in our introduction , there’s not a ton of wiggle room in the Brewers’ infield, except for one notable exception. That exception is at first base, where we see the one place on the roster that a big hole was taken out of the 2026 World Series-winning club after Jake Bauers left for Boston in free agency. Before we get to that, let’s quickly recap where things sit at the other infield positions, where things look to be set for the forseeable future. Brice Turang, one of the best players in the league, is locked in at second base and is under team control through 2029. Cooper Pratt, at shortstop, is under team control through 2033 with two additional club options. Unless a trade happens (not out of the question!), Milwaukee will almost certainly start the season with a platoon of Joey Ortiz and David Hamilton at third base; both players are arbitration-eligible for the first time in 2026, and, like Turang, would hit free agency after the 2029 season. Of course, no one is under any illusions that this infield will look like it does right now for the next three years even if everyone is under contract, and that’s because one of the game’s top prospects, Jesús Made, is coming. Made played the entire 2026 season at Double-A Biloxi and it seems likely that he’ll start the 2026 season at Triple-A Nashville. But Made’s career has, in many ways, mirrored Jackson Chourio’s, and when Chourio was at the same point in his career, he signed a 10-year contract and was on the Opening Day roster. The Brewers are surely thinking about offering a similar type of contract to Made, if they haven’t already, and if he accepts, it’s not out of the question that he could start the year in the majors—especially if the start of the season is delayed due to the lockout. top.title: Jets Watch: Utah’s Power Play Could Expose One of Winnipeg’s Biggest Weaknesses
top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Winnipeg Jets have earned points in eight of their past nine games, but Monday’s matchup against the Utah Mammoth could test one of their biggest weaknesses. Utah has one of the NHL’s most dangerous power plays, while the Jets have struggled to kill penalties. If the Jets spend too much time shorthanded, their recent improvement at even strength might not be enough. Utah has won two straight after going six games without a victory and swept all three meetings with the Jets last season. Both teams had Sunday off ahead of Monday’s game at Canada Life Centre. The Jets are trying to finish their homestand with a win before heading east, while Utah is looking to build on its recent success. Utah’s Power Play Presents a Serious Challenge The matchup on special teams may run this game. Utah has scored 27 power-play goals on 83 opportunities this season, converting at 32.5%, the third-best rate in the NHL. The Jets, meanwhile, have killed just 72.5% of their penalties, ranking 24th. They’ve allowed 19 power-play goals in 69 times shorthanded, making this a concerning matchup for a team that has already struggled to keep pucks out of its net down a man. Utah’s power play has been responsible for roughly 34% of its total goals this season, and much of that production has come from its top unit. According to Primitive Stats , Utah’s established top power-play unit of Nick Schmaltz, Logan Cooley, Clayton Keller, Dylan Guenther and Mikhail Sergachev has generated 9.28 expected goals per 60 minutes across nearly 60 minutes together. That combination has scored 16 goals while sharing the ice on the power play. Utah’s potential absences don’t necessarily mean the Jets will catch a break. Utah’s penalty kill has also struggled, operating at 71.3%, so the Jets could have chances to take advantage at the other end. top.title: The birth of 'Iron' Mike: Inside the night Tyson became boxing's youngest heavyweight champion, 40 years later
top.description: Looking back on it 40 years later, you miss the tuxedos for the occasion. The HBO broadcast crew of Barry Tompkins, “Sugar” Ray Leonard and Larry Merchant, in their finest evening dress, dapper down to the cufflinks, gathered at the Las Vegas Hilton for what Merchant called a “coronation more than a contest.” On Nov. 22, 1986, Mike Tyson, just 20 years and four months old, was set to become boxing’s youngest ever heavyweight world champion. It felt like a chandelier affair, even if, as Tompkins points out, it was in fact the “diametric opposite.” Tyson, a kid from the Brooklyn who’d been taken under wing by Cus D’Amato, stalked toward the boxing ring for his title bout with Trevor Berbick wearing his trademark white towel as a shirt, crudely slit down the middle to slip over his head. He was in the iconic black trunks, which would earn him a $5,000 fine for insubordination because Berbick had elected to wear black, and Mike wasn’t yet the champion. The heightened sense of anticipation belonged to that word: Yet . Invincibility is a fool’s notion, after all, while inevitability is straight terror. Even at 20 years old — especially at 20 — Tyson brokered in the kind of doom that could do 50 shares for HBO, which means that 50% of all households with HBO would tune in. He dealt in the kind of doom that didn’t belong to the tamer confines of sport, but to a savagery that instead delved deeper into man’s innermost darkness. Fighting from the shell, he would hold his palms at his chin and nuzzle into his opponent, only to explode from the inside with an uppercut or right hook, from his legs through the knuckle, and from the cruelest of angles, to snap a man’s head back from his shoulders. Mike Tyson (L) had 15 fights in his debut year as a professional, winning all by knockout. Andy Hayt via Getty Images Everyone knew Berbick, the WBC heavyweight champion heading into what was being billed as the Heavyweight World Series, was in well over his head. There was the one against Joe Frazier’s son, Marvis Frazier, where the “myth of Tyson” — as HBO’s longtime blow-by-blow man Jim Lampley believes — really began. top.title: The Toronto Maple Leafs’ Collapse Started Years Ago. Firing Jim Hiller Won’t Fix It.
top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Toronto Maple Leafs have spent much of the past decade trying to figure out why a team with so much talent has accomplished so little when it matters most. Coaches have come and gone, executives have been replaced, and the roster has undergone significant changes. Yet somehow, the Leafs keep finding themselves back in the same conversation. Now, with another miserable stretch of hockey putting the organization under the microscope, the question is once again what needs to change. But there’s something worth considering before the Leafs decide who deserves the blame this time. What if their problems aren’t nearly as new as they appear? A look through the past 10 seasons of the Leafs’ underlying numbers suggests they’ve been moving in the wrong direction for years. And for a while, their results were good enough to hide it. The Maple Leafs Have Been Losing Ground for Years During the 2021-22 season, the Leafs were one of the NHL’s strongest teams at 5-on-5. According to Natural Stat Trick, they controlled 55.24% of expected goals. That’s an excellent number over an 82-game season. The Leafs scored 208 goals and allowed 182 at 5-on-5, and there was plenty of reason to believe they could compete with just about anybody. The problem is that the Leafs haven’t been able to sustain that level of play. Their 5-on-5 expected-goals share dropped to 53.54% in 2022-23, then 51.54% in 2023-24. By 2024-25, they were down to 48.52%, meaning opponents were generating better scoring chances over the course of the season. It wasn’t a sudden collapse. Their share of expected goals declined for four consecutive seasons, eventually reaching 45.67% in 2025-26. And while the changes behind the bench and in the front office understandably attracted attention, the numbers suggest the decline was already underway. The Maple Leafs’ Success in 2024-25 Hid a Serious Problem During the 2024-25 season, the Leafs scored 169 goals and allowed just 136 at 5-on-5. That’s a goal differential of plus-33, and they accounted for 55.41% of the goals scored when the teams were playing at even strength. Those are the kinds of numbers you’d expect from a team controlling games, except the Leafs weren’t. They generated 159.04 expected goals and allowed 168.75, giving them a negative expected-goals differential of 9.71. They were being outchanced in terms of quality, yet finished the season outscoring opponents by 33 goals. That’s a swing of more than 42 goals between their actual differential and what their expected-goals numbers suggested. Of course, there’s a pretty obvious reason the Leafs might be able to outperform their expected-goals numbers: Auston Matthews . PETERSBURG, FL - OCTOBER 28: Jake Bauers #9 of the Milwaukee Brewers poses for a photo with The Commissioner's Trophy in the clubhouse following Game Five of the 2026 World Series presented by Capital One between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field on Wednesday, October 28, 2026 in St. Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Daniel Shirey/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images The votes are in for our No. 5 spot in this year’s MVBrewers rankings, and it’s a former Brewer in the form of first baseman Jake Bauers. Bauers, who signed with the Red Sox just over a week ago, garnered 65 of the 106 total votes (61.3%), easily beating Aaron Ashby (31 votes), Trevor Megill (five votes), Garrett Mitchell (three votes), Abner Uribe (one vote), and Sal Frelick (one write-in vote from @mlv234). Bauers, now 31, is coming off what was easily the best season of his career. After totaling negative WAR over the first six seasons of his career with the Rays, Indians (Guardians), Mariners, Yankees, and Brewers, he played in a career-high 144 games in 2026, hitting .266/.389/.484 with a team-high 26 homers, 22 doubles, 86 RBIs, 93 runs, and 11 steals. His 140 OPS+ was also far and away the best of his career, outpacing the 111 mark he put up in 2025. While he was slightly below average defensively, he served as a key cog in Pat Murphy’s lineups, earning a Silver Slugger at the utility position. His ability to draw walks was particularly elite, as he had a 16.3% walk rate, ranking in the 98th percentile. He also ranked in the top 10% in xwOBA (.371), average exit velocity (92.1 mph), barrel rate (14.0%), hard-hit rate (51.9%), launch angle sweet-spot rate (38.6%), bat speed (76.5 mph), and chase rate (21.7%). In the postseason, Bauers continued to draw walks, even as he struggled to collect hits in the World Series. He was especially good in the NLCS, earning MVP honors as he hit .286/.412/.571 with both of those extra-base hits, all six RBIs, and three walks. As with just about every other player on the Brewers, Bauers had a signature moment in the postseason — in fact, he had two. Wabara argued that the opposition’s strength lay not in the number of presidential candidates contesting against one another but in its ability to unite behind one candidate with the political capacity, national reach and popular support to challenge the APC. nigeria.title: UK Digging New Reservoirs To Fight Persistent Droughts
nigeria.description: Britain has long had a reputation for rain. But as it adapts to a warmer, drier climate, the UK is racing to complete a huge new reservoir, its first in over three decades. Bulldozers have been digging up the ground for the vast £800-million ($1 billion) Havant Thicket project near the southern coastal port of Portsmouth. Like much of Europe, Britain endured record-breaking heat this summer and, despite the return of rains as the country moves into winter, parts are still grappling with drought conditions. “We’ve got increasing problems with our water security in the UK,” climate scientist Hannah Cloke from Reading University told AFP. “We need to really think about how we’re storing that water because this problem is only going to get worse.” Scientists have warned extreme weather events are likely to become more frequent and more intense as the global climate changes. Workers carry out construction work at the site of the new Havant Thicket Reservoir in Hampshire, southern England, on November 5, 2026. Photo by CARLOS JASSO / AFP By mid-November, almost all of England remained in drought, with some areas classified as suffering severe drought, according to the Environment Agency. Potentially exacerbating matters, existing reservoirs were only 60 percent full, 19 percentage points below the seasonal average. For policymakers, the situation poses a longer-term challenge as the thirst for water increases with a rising population and the growth of heavy water-using industries such as data centres. Under England’s National Framework for Water Resources published in 2025, the country could face a daily water supply shortfall of five billion litres (1.3 billion gallons) by 2055, with resources under pressure. At the sprawling Havant Thicket site, Portsmouth Water chief executive Bob Taylor said the industry was waking up to the scale of the challenge after successive droughts and hot summers. Workers carry out construction work at the site of the new Havant Thicket Reservoir in Hampshire, southern England, on November 5, 2026. Photo by CARLOS JASSO / AFP The issue, he stressed, was not necessarily how much rain falls over the course of a year, but when it falls. Winters are becoming wetter, while summers are increasingly dry. “Without reservoirs you can’t store that intense rainfall and put it somewhere where it can be used at another time,” Taylor said. The new reservoir will eventually hold up to 8.7 billion litres of water, helping secure supplies for hundreds of thousands of people. Fed in part by winter surpluses from a major spring already tapped by Portsmouth Water, it has become one of the flagship projects in a broader shift in Britain’s water strategy. The government has approved the construction of nine major reservoirs by 2050, and last year relaxed planning rules to speed up projects after decades of under-investment in water infrastructure. Together, the future reservoirs could deliver an additional 670 million litres of water per day. ‘

Former military chief Eisenkot has until December 6 — a deadline which can be extended by 14 days — to form a government to replace Netanyahu after the October election failed to deliver a clear majority for either bloc. Delegations from Eisenkot’s centrist Yashar party and Netanyahu’s right-wing Likud are due to meet on Monday evening for a third round of negotiations, a spokesperson for Likud told AFP. Representatives from each party met for nearly four hours on Sunday and laid out their positions “on a range of substantive issues,” with no sign of a breakthrough. – Political ‘boycotts’ – On Saturday, Yashar presented the talks as “a genuine commitment to forming the broadest possible government”, saying that Eisenkot had asked his representatives to explore all options. Likud immediately laid down several conditions for its participation in a unity government, including an end to “all personal attacks” and political “boycotts” targeting Netanyahu and his government. Eisenkot’s 48-member bloc needs 61 lawmakers to reach a majority and remains divided over how to build a coalition. Short of 61 lawmakers, Eisenkot’s bloc could form a minority government. The head of the left-leaning Democrats party, Yair Golan, on Monday called for an end to the “sham talks with Likud”. Netanyahu is pushing for a national unity government, which could see a rotation of the premiership between the two men, a mechanism already tried in Israel. Such an arrangement could allow Netanyahu to keep his political leverage against the corruption charges he faces, as well as continue to oppose the creation of an independent commission of inquiry into the security failures that preceded the Hamas attack of October 7, 2023. But that prospect runs up against Eisenkot’s refusal to serve in a cabinet led by Netanyahu, against whom he centred his campaign. Last week, Eisenkot said that he would be prepared to put forward a minority national emergency government for a parliamentary vote should efforts to create a broad-based government fail. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. Read the full recipe for Rice and Peas with Oxtail . Rice and peas with oxtail, from Episode 1 Soliat Bada and Michael Famoroti in Episode 1 Episode 2 moves to the Gulf for lamb kabsa, Saudi Arabia’s national dish, fragrant with dried lime and seven spice. Soliat is joined by Bella Adeleke , CEO of Asali Africa and founder of the fashion label Garbe, for a conversation about redefining success. Read the full recipe for Lamb Kabsa . Lamb kabsa, from Episode 2 Still to come are Nigerian fried rice with fried turkey and dodo, cooked with Toyin Jolapamo and Nneoma Mere; jambalaya with Goldie Iyamu and Vanessa Iloenyosi ; and a season finale with Edwin Okolo and Temi Omolehinwa. For more on Asali Africa and the products and ideas it develops, visit asali.africa . Episodes 1 and 2 are out now on YouTube. entertainment.title: Beyond the Mini LED Label: What Should Define Good Mini LED Performance?
entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? Where TCL Enters The Category Conversation TCL is relevant to that discussion because Mini LED has become a significant part of its global television business. According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. TCL reported 2.43 million Mini LED TV shipments during the period, representing 77.1% year on year growth. That position follows a strong 2025, when TCL reported, based on Omdia data, a 31.1% share of global Mini LED TV shipments and 118.0% year on year shipment growth. Market scale does not, on its own, define technology leadership. What it does provide is evidence that a manufacturer has become an important participant in how the category develops. For a company operating at that scale, leadership increasingly includes helping make the technology easier to understand and giving consumers clearer ways to evaluate what they are buying. entertainment.title: A Safari, a Beach & Easy Entry? 5 African Spots for Your Christmas Holiday
entertainment.description: Five African destinations Nigerian passport holders can visit visa-free or with visa on arrival this Christmas holiday. Image: AI-generated. The group chat has the concerts, the dinners and the Detty December link-ups covered. But has anyone planned the getaway? Beyond the usual Lagos parties and end-of-year outings, there is a whole continent waiting to be explored, with sun-soaked beaches, wildlife safaris, exciting food scenes and cities with plenty of stories to tell. You do not have to spend weeks navigating embassy appointments and visa applications to make it happen, either. Several African countries offer Nigerian passport holders visa-free entry or visas on arrival, making a festive-season escape much easier to plan. Whether you are travelling solo, gathering your friends, taking the family along or joining a curated travel group, here are five destinations worth considering for your Christmas holiday. Kenya Imagine spotting lions and giraffes against a city skyline before breakfast, then catching an evening flight or train straight to the coast for fresh seafood by the Indian Ocean. That contrast is what makes Kenya such a rewarding December escape. Nairobi gives you immediate access to wildlife at Nairobi National Park and the Giraffe Centre alongside lively restaurants and art spaces in Westlands and Karen, while longer itineraries open up classic game drives in the Maasai Mara, views of Mount Kilimanjaro in Amboseli, and warm beach days in Diani or Watamu. Nigerian citizens enjoy visa-free entry for short stays of up to 60 days without needing a paid eTA, leaving more room in your budget for safaris and coastal stays. Rwanda Not everyone wants their year-end holiday to feel like a non-stop sprint, and Rwanda is built for travellers who prefer scenery, clean air, and an unhurried pace. Days in Kigali easily revolve around specialty coffee shops, contemporary art at Inema Arts Center, and a sobering, essential visit to the Kigali Genocide Memorial before you head out into the countryside. From the capital, you can track chimpanzees and walk above the trees in Nyungwe Forest, go on wildlife drives in Akagera National Park, or spend quiet afternoons along the shores of Lake Kivu. With 30-day visa-free entry for Nigerian passport holders, getting there is straightforward from start to finish. Mauritius Sometimes a proper Christmas break calls for leaving mainland schedules behind altogether for turquoise lagoons, catamaran cruises, and mountain trails. In Mauritius, you can base yourself around Grand Baie in the north for boat trips to Île aux Cerfs and lively beachside dinners, or head south-west toward Le Morne Brabant for coastal hikes and water sports. Between beach days, the bustling Central Market in Port Louis, the lush trails of Black River Gorges National Park, and Casela Nature Parks keep a week-long itinerary full without ever feeling hectic. entertainment.title: Esther Adeyanju: This International Men’s Day, Let’s Make Room for Men’s Vulnerability
entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? Surely, a man’s worth cannot be reduced to his bank balance, job title or ability to convince everyone that he has everything under control. There must be room for men who are still becoming. entertainment.title: How La Roche-Posay Brought Skin Science to Over 500 Guests in Its First Living Lab Experience
entertainment.description: La Roche-Posay concluded its first Living Lab experience in Nigeria, welcoming Nigerian stakeholders to its opening party and three-day programme, held from 4 to 6 November 2026 at Oasis by The Five Palm, Victoria Island, Lagos. Inspired by the original Living Lab concept in Paris, the experience brought the science, research and expertise behind skincare closer to Nigerian consumers and healthcare professionals. It marked the brand’s first Living Lab in the country, creating a platform for more accessible conversations around skin health, dermatological innovation and everyday skincare. The experience opened with an exclusive session for healthcare professionals and invited guests before welcoming members of the public over the following two days. Each day featured three expert-led sessions exploring the role of dermatology and scientific research in advancing skin health, the wider impact of skin conditions on everyday life, and the importance of understanding product safety, tolerance and efficacy. The sessions brought together healthcare professionals and representatives from across Nigeria’s dermatological beauty and skincare community, encouraging knowledge-sharing and stronger connections between science, expertise and consumer education. Visitors explored five dedicated Innovation Corners showcasing La Roche-Posay’s Effaclar, Mela B3, Anthelios, Cicaplast and Lipikar ranges. Each space introduced visitors to specific skin concerns and the science behind the brand’s product formulations. Through interactive demonstrations and guided product experiences, guests gained a better understanding of different skin concerns and the role of targeted skincare in addressing them. At the Anthelios corner, visitors used a UV camera to see the effects of ultraviolet exposure and better understand the importance of sun protection. The Effaclar and Mela B3 spaces explored concerns including blemishes and hyperpigmentation, while the Cicaplast and Lipikar corners introduced visitors to approaches to caring for sensitive, damaged and dry skin. Beyond the Innovation Corners, visitors explored the Blue House, which presented La Roche-Posay’s history and commitment to dermatological innovation, and the Scars of Life Cinema. The cinema screened a 25-minute film exploring the physical and psychological realities of living with scars and scarring, including their impact on self-image and everyday life. The film also highlighted how Lipikar supports the care of skin affected by scarring, bringing attention to the importance of addressing both the visible and less visible experiences associated with skin conditions. The programme also created opportunities for visitors to engage with skincare experts and dermatologists through one-on-one consultations, ask questions about their individual skin concerns and receive guidance on building appropriate skincare routines. entertainment.description: One of the best aspects of art is its ability to imitate current events or imagine possibilities. Movies, as a powerful art form, present a sequence of events that allows viewers to see reflections of themselves or envision who they could become. At its core, art exists to entertain, inform and critique society. Through films, music and visual expressions, we are continually reminded of our shared humanity—our joys, flaws and contradictions. One subject that art, particularly film, has explored is masculinity. However, this theme is often addressed subtly and can be easy to overlook, as the movies that dominate global box offices frequently focus on spectacle: fantasy, romance, adventure or others. Conversations about men, their inner lives, vulnerabilities and social roles are often not in the top circle. Nonetheless, some films have attempted to explore what it means to be a man in today’s world. They invite audiences to contemplate important questions such as: What is the role of men in society? What defines a man? How does a man’s behaviour influence those around him? What expectations does society place on men? What responsibilities do men have within society? Where does responsibility begin, and where does it end? Do men matter? Do their feelings matter? The theme for this year’s International Men’s Day is “The Future Is For Everyone.” For that, here are some movies that explore and illuminate the complexities of masculinity: The Pursuit of Happyness This classic film reveals the vulnerability often hidden behind male perseverance. Will Smith ’s portrayal of Chris Gardner challenges the stoic notion of manhood by showing fatherhood as both an act of love and endurance. Through his struggles with homelessness, rejection, and exhaustion, the film redefines masculinity, depicting it as the courage to remain tender even when life tests your strength in every way. Fatherhood Kevin Hart ’s film Fatherhood delves into themes of grief and single parenthood, balancing humour with heartfelt moments. It challenges traditional expectations of masculinity by illustrating a father’s journey through uncertainty, learning empathy, and committing to being present for his child/ren. Through this film, Kevin Hart shares his vision of what it means to be a man and a father. entertainment.description: What does it really mean to play to win in business and leadership? Beyond earning a seat at the table, it requires more than competence or professional accomplishments. It requires the confidence to own one’s value, the clarity to communicate one’s contributions and the intentionality to build visibility that translates into meaningful influence. These conversations defined The Executive Woman Summit (TEWS) 2.0 , which brought together hundreds of executive women, corporate professionals, entrepreneurs and emerging leaders at Harbour Point, Victoria Island, Lagos, on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. Convened by Bola Matel-Okoh , a dual-qualified attorney (called to both the New York and Nigerian Bars), Executive Coach, Non-Executive Director at Wema Bank, and CEO of BMO Advisory Services , the second edition of the summit was themed Playing to Win: Elevate Your Vision, Value and Visibility. It provided an intentional platform for candid conversations, practical insights and strategic alliances on what it takes for women to advance, lead and thrive in today’s evolving corporate landscape. In her opening address, Matel-Okoh challenged women to rethink how they approach professional visibility, authority and advancement. According to her, competence is merely the baseline; it is not enough if you are unwilling to communicate your value, own your voice and position yourself for higher-stakes opportunities. This philosophy also came through in her cover interview with THISDAY Glitterati ahead of the summit, where she offered a compelling perspective on the distinction between holding a powerful position and exercising genuine influence. “A powerful position gives you formal authority. Influence determines how deeply your leadership shapes people’s thinking, decisions and actions. A title may secure your place in a meeting, but credibility makes people listen,” she explained. She also challenged the assumption that excellent work will automatically speak for itself, encouraging women to communicate their contributions with evidence and confidence. “What problem did you solve? What result did you produce? What changed because of your leadership?” she asked, highlighting the importance of making professional value visible to the decision-makers who influence career progression and boardroom opportunities. “There is no need to diminish your achievements to make others comfortable. You can be gracious and still be clear about the value you bring,” she added. sports.description: Super Bowl weekend did not disappoint. It started with Hendricken and La Salle’s sellout showdown at Beirne Stadium on Friday night and ended with Juanita Sanchez ’s historic win over Scituate on Saturday night. Four great games with four terrific performances from all the teams involved. Was it easy to find nominees for the Providence Journal Super Bowl Player of the Week? Yes. Was it hard to pick five? It always is, but we managed to do it. So who will earn the honor? We’ll leave that up to our readers, who will vote to decide the Providence Journal Super Bowl Player of the Week. There’s only one way to vote - check out the bios of this week’s five nominees and then make you pick in the ballot at the bottom of the page. Voting opens Monday morning and runs through Saturday and you can vote as many times as you’d like between then. What does Player of the Week receive? The prize for Providence Journal Football Player of the Week is simple – it’s a big bucket of clout. sports.title: Differing account of ‘gentleman’s agreement’ between Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala as plot thickens
sports.description: (Photo by Harry Langer/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images The latest reporting from Sky Germany’s Florian Plettenberg (via @iMiaSanMia ) adds another layer to the increasingly complicated discussion surrounding Jamal Musiala’s contract at Bayern Munich, particula rly when compared with the earlier report that Bayern believes a “gentleman’s agreement” with Musiala’s camp has been violated. According to Plettenberg, Uli Hoeneß met with Musiala’s agency at Tegernsee in August 2026. The meeting took place before Musiala’s condition was publicly disclosed and before his two collapses during the friendly matches against Leipzig and Heidenheim. Hoeneß was reportedly informed of Musiala’s health condition at the time, and the meeting was described as having taken place in a positive, trusting atmosphere. However, the crucial detail is what reportedly did not happen: no specific agre ements were reached regarding a potential contract adjustment if Musiala’s performan ces declined, and no assurances were made, either verbally or in writing. This new information appears to complicate the narrative outlined in the Süddeutsche Zeitung report that prompted our earlier coverage. That report claimed two legally non-binding gentlemen’s agreements were reached during a summer meeting between Hoeneß and Musiala’s agent, Christian Schmid — Bayern Munich would support Musiala through his recovery, and the contract could be adjusted in Bayern’s favor if Musiala continued to struggle with his health and medication side effects. The distinction between the two accounts is significant. The earlier report suggested an understanding existed regarding a possible contr actual adjustment if Musiala could not return to his previous level. Plettenberg’s reporting, however, expli citly denies that any such agreement, assurance, or commitment was made. That does not necessarily mean the two reports are entirely incomp atible. There could have been discussions about Musiala’s health, expectations, and the club’s concerns without eithe r party reaching a concrete understanding about modifying the contract. Even so, the latest reporting directly challenges the idea that Musiala’s camp agreed to a specific contingency involving his salary. Like every other aspect of this saga, we know some things, but not enough. For now, Bayern Munich’s frustration may be real, but the precise nature of any alleged gentleman’s agreement remains disputed—and that distinction matters enormously in this increasingly contentious saga. sports.title: Jets Watch: Utah’s Power Play Could Expose One of Winnipeg’s Biggest Weaknesses
sports.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Winnipeg Jets have earned points in eight of their past nine games, but Monday’s matchup against the Utah Mammoth could test one of their biggest weaknesses. Utah has one of the NHL’s most dangerous power plays, while the Jets have struggled to kill penalties. If the Jets spend too much time shorthanded, their recent improvement at even strength might not be enough. Utah has won two straight after going six games without a victory and swept all three meetings with the Jets last season. Both teams had Sunday off ahead of Monday’s game at Canada Life Centre. The Jets are trying to finish their homestand with a win before heading east, while Utah is looking to build on its recent success. Utah’s Power Play Presents a Serious Challenge The matchup on special teams may run this game. Utah has scored 27 power-play goals on 83 opportunities this season, converting at 32.5%, the third-best rate in the NHL. The Jets, meanwhile, have killed just 72.5% of their penalties, ranking 24th. They’ve allowed 19 power-play goals in 69 times shorthanded, making this a concerning matchup for a team that has already struggled to keep pucks out of its net down a man. sports.title: The birth of 'Iron' Mike: Inside the night Tyson became boxing's youngest heavyweight champion, 40 years later
sports.description: Looking back on it 40 years later, you miss the tuxedos for the occasion. The HBO broadcast crew of Barry Tompkins, “Sugar” Ray Leonard and Larry Merchant, in their finest evening dress, dapper down to the cufflinks, gathered at the Las Vegas Hilton for what Merchant called a “coronation more than a contest.” On Nov. 22, 1986, Mike Tyson, just 20 years and four months old, was set to become boxing’s youngest ever heavyweight world champion. It felt like a chandelier affair, even if, as Tompkins points out, it was in fact the “diametric opposite.” Tyson, a kid from the Brooklyn who’d been taken under wing by Cus D’Amato, stalked toward the boxing ring for his title bout with Trevor Berbick wearing his trademark white towel as a shirt, crudely slit down the middle to slip over his head. He was in the iconic black trunks, which would earn him a $5,000 fine for insubordination because Berbick had elected to wear black, and Mike wasn’t yet the champion. The heightened sense of anticipation belonged to that word: Yet . Invincibility is a fool’s notion, after all, while inevitability is straight terror. Even at 20 years old — especially at 20 — Tyson brokered in the kind of doom that could do 50 shares for HBO, which means that 50% of all households with HBO would tune in. He dealt in the kind of doom that didn’t belong to the tamer confines of sport, but to a savagery that instead delved deeper into man’s innermost darkness. Fighting from the shell, he would hold his palms at his chin and nuzzle into his opponent, only to explode from the inside with an uppercut or right hook, from his legs through the knuckle, and from the cruelest of angles, to snap a man’s head back from his shoulders. Mike Tyson (L) had 15 fights in his debut year as a professional, winning all by knockout. Andy Hayt via Getty Images Everyone knew Berbick, the WBC heavyweight champion heading into what was being billed as the Heavyweight World Series, was in well over his head. Berbick, considered a decent enough defensive strategist, would need to incorporate something more like self-preservation to survive against Tyson, who by November had already won a dozen fights that year alone. There was the one against Joe Frazier’s son, Marvis Frazier, where the “myth of Tyson” — as HBO’s longtime blow-by-blow man Jim Lampley believes — really began. sports.title: The Toronto Maple Leafs’ Collapse Started Years Ago. Firing Jim Hiller Won’t Fix It.
sports.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Toronto Maple Leafs have spent much of the past decade trying to figure out why a team with so much talent has accomplished so little when it matters most. Coaches have come and gone, executives have been replaced, and the roster has undergone significant changes. Yet somehow, the Leafs keep finding themselves back in the same conversation. Now, with another miserable stretch of hockey putting the organization under the microscope, the question is once again what needs to change. But there’s something worth considering before the Leafs decide who deserves the blame this time. What if their problems aren’t nearly as new as they appear? A look through the past 10 seasons of the Leafs’ underlying numbers suggests they’ve been moving in the wrong direction for years. And for a while, their results were good enough to hide it. The Maple Leafs Have Been Losing Ground for Years During the 2021-22 season, the Leafs were one of the NHL’s strongest teams at 5-on-5. According to Natural Stat Trick, they controlled 55.24% of expected goals. That’s an excellent number over an 82-game season. The Leafs scored 208 goals and allowed 182 at 5-on-5, and there was plenty of reason to believe they could compete with just about anybody. The problem is that the Leafs haven’t been able to sustain that level of play. Their 5-on-5 expected-goals share dropped to 53.54% in 2022-23, then 51.54% in 2023-24. By 2024-25, they were down to 48.52%, meaning opponents were generating better scoring chances over the course of the season. It wasn’t a sudden collapse. Their share of expected goals declined for four consecutive seasons, eventually reaching 45.67% in 2025-26. And while the changes behind the bench and in the front office understandably attracted attention, the numbers suggest the decline was already underway. The Maple Leafs’ Success in 2024-25 Hid a Serious Problem During the 2024-25 season, the Leafs scored 169 goals and allowed just 136 at 5-on-5. That’s a goal differential of plus-33, and they accounted for 55.41% of the goals scored when the teams were playing at even strength. Those are the kinds of numbers you’d expect from a team controlling games, except the Leafs weren’t. They generated 159.04 expected goals and allowed 168.75, giving them a negative expected-goals differential of 9.71. They were being outchanced in terms of quality, yet finished the season outscoring opponents by 33 goals. That’s a swing of more than 42 goals between their actual differential and what their expected-goals numbers suggested. Of course, there’s a pretty obvious reason the Leafs might be able to outperform their expected-goals numbers: Auston Matthews . Expected goals measure the likelihood of a shot becoming a goal based on factors such as location and shot type. The first is the zone defense. The second is a point guard who controls every aspect of the game and gets the Warriors a bucket when they need it. Juvaris Hayes, Javon Bennett, Budd Clark, and most recently Kevair Kennedy have all filled that role for Joe Gallo. So far this season, that role has been a void. And yes, it took a minute for Kennedy to truly emerge last season, but it’s quite simple. The Warriors’ offense is not getting enough out of its floor generals. And it might be because of the old adage: “If you have two quarterbacks, you have no quarterbacks.” Jeremiah, Ayden, both, or neither Freshman Ayden Johnson has started all five games for Merrimack. He is averaging 6.6 points, 2.6 assists and 1.6 rebounds per game. Fifth-year senior Jeremiah Anderson, a transfer from Division-II Felician, has come off the bench averaging 7.2 points, 3.0 rebounds and 0.6 assists. That’s not nearly enough production from two players Merrimack’s usage leader is Denver Anglin at 26%. Anglin attempts more than two-thirds of his shots from behind the arc, has attempted just eight foul shots all year, and has four assists in five games. That’s just not what we’ve come to expect out of a high-usage Merrimack guard. Johnson’s usage rate? Just 17.4%. And he hasn’t exactly earned more usage either – the freshman has just a 43.7 true shooting percentage. Anderson has a higher usage rate at 25.4% but hasn’t been much of a playmaker. sports.description: ST. PETERSBURG, FL - OCTOBER 28: Jake Bauers #9 of the Milwaukee Brewers poses for a photo with The Commissioner's Trophy in the clubhouse following Game Five of the 2026 World Series presented by Capital One between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field on Wednesday, October 28, 2026 in St. Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Daniel Shirey/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images The votes are in for our No. 5 spot in this year’s MVBrewers rankings, and it’s a former Brewer in the form of first baseman Jake Bauers. Bauers, who signed with the Red Sox just over a week ago, garnered 65 of the 106 total votes (61.3%), easily beating Aaron Ashby (31 votes), Trevor Megill (five votes), Garrett Mitchell (three votes), Abner Uribe (one vote), and Sal Frelick (one write-in vote from @mlv234). Bauers, now 31, is coming off what was easily the best season of his career. After totaling negative WAR over the first six seasons of his career with the Rays, Indians (Guardians), Mariners, Yankees, and Brewers, he played in a career-high 144 games in 2026, hitting .266/.389/.484 with a team-high 26 homers, 22 doubles, 86 RBIs, 93 runs, and 11 steals. His 140 OPS+ was also far and away the best of his career, outpacing the 111 mark he put up in 2025. While he was slightly below average defensively, he served as a key cog in Pat Murphy’s lineups, earning a Silver Slugger at the utility position. His ability to draw walks was particularly elite, as he had a 16.3% walk rate, ranking in the 98th percentile. He also ranked in the top 10% in xwOBA (.371), average exit velocity (92.1 mph), barrel rate (14.0%), hard-hit rate (51.9%), launch angle sweet-spot rate (38.6%), bat speed (76.5 mph), and chase rate (21.7%). In the postseason, Bauers continued to draw walks, even as he struggled to collect hits in the World Series. He finished the playoffs hitting .191/.345/.277 with a homer, a double, six RBIs, four runs, and 10 walks. He was especially good in the NLCS, earning MVP honors as he hit .286/.412/.571 with both of those extra-base hits, all six RBIs, and three walks. As with just about every other player on the Brewers, Bauers had a signature moment in the postseason — in fact, he had two. First, it was a huge 12-pitch walk against Yoshinobu Yamamoto in NLCS Game 2 , loading the bases for Christian Yelich, who promptly singled a pair home to give Milwaukee a 3-2 lead. 2026 PitchingNinja Award for At Bat of the Year ending in a Walk. 🏆 Winner: Jake Bauers' Epic 12 Pitch Walk pic.twitter.com/eSD7G5HlPP — Rob Friedman (@PitchingNinja) November 21, 2026 Just two days later, it was Bauers facing off with Blake Snell in the seventh inning of NLCS Game 3 . This time, Bauers saw 11 pitches, and on that 11th pitch, he slugged a huge two-run homer, flipping the scoreboard to give Milwaukee a 3-2 lead they wouldn’t relinquish. 2026 PitchingNinja Award for At Bat of the Year ending in a Home Run. 🏆 Winner: Jake Bauers' Epic 11 Pitch AB HR.

sports.description: (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images There’s something in the water when it comes to wide receivers in Pittsburgh that turns them into clowns. It’s been this way since the halcyon days of Hines Ward, as the team has managed, time and time and time again, to be saddled with problematic guys and know exactly when to part ways before the ticking time bomb explodes. Until DK Metcalf arrived. This is the organization’s big mistake, the whiff that is setting them back, and Sunday was a perfect example of how much of a disaster Metcalf has been for this team. It isn’t simply about losing to a hopeless Eagles team, or Metcalf getting ejected for poking Cooper DeJean in the eye , or even losing pace in the AFC North — it’s all of these things in concert, and the fact that they’re paying through the moon for this guy to actively hurt their team. Perhaps the worst part of all this is that anyone could see this was a HORRIBLE move for the Steelers when they made it. Receivers are mercurial. No position in sports is more based on vibes and emotions than WR, and the second a receiver loses their confidence or stops getting fed, the majority will pitch a fit like an ornery toddler you forgot to bring snacks for. Metcalf was a reliable 1,000-yard guy in Seattle because of how he played the game. The Seahawks established everything through their run game, then used Metcalf to generate explosive plays downfield. This is why he averaged over 15 yards per catch downfield and had a reputation as the best deep ball guy in the NFL. What a receiver with a penchant for deep throws shouldn’t fool anyone: Deep throws. *Gasp*, I know it’s a shocker — but you kind of need a guy with a big enough arm to stretch the field to get the best out of Metcalf’s skillset. Know what old-man Aaron Rodgers doesn’t have? A big arm. At no point during any of his career was Rodgers an elite deep passer. He was always known for his intelligence on intermediate routes and an incredible ability to find the open man when operating out of structure. There was never a chance Metcalf was going to be a good fit for this iteration of the Steelers, and it’s been a wreck. Metcalf had a career-low 59 receptions in 2025, for a career-low 850 yards. In 2026 he’s trending towards having 61 receptions this season, a new career low of 738 yards, and another new career low of 3 TDs. technology.title: Old-school Linux desktops find fresh routes to Wayland
technology.description: Xfce's next release is taking shape for 2027, while MATE users have fresh options for moving their familiar desktop onto Wayland. One of the oldest surviving Linux desktops has a relatively slow release schedule: new stable releases of Xfce tend to appear every two years. The project just updated its release engineering roadmap for the forthcoming Xfce 4.22, and it looks like the next version won't arrive until early next year. We covered the release of Xfce 4.20 in December 2024, but 4.22 is still incubating. The roadmap schedules its first prerelease and feature freeze for December 15, 2026, followed by a second prerelease on January 15, 2027. A third prerelease is optional, and neither that nor the final release has a date. February or March might be plausible, but that's our guess, not the project's promise. The Xfce developers tend not to rush into things. Wayland development continues in 4.22, building on the preliminary support in 4.20. The team is also working on its own compositor, xfwl4, although the roadmap doesn't promise feature parity with X11. (In Wayland terminology, the "compositor" is the combined display server and window manager.) The compositor has its own development roadmap . The name is a nod to the current Xfce X11 window manager, which is called xfwm4 . The main developer of the new xfwl4 compositor is Brian Tarricone , who has been working on other parts of Xfce since 2004. Back in July, he shared a blog post about his use of generative-AI coding assistants called LLMs and xfwl4 . He says: "So yes, I use Claude quite a bit while developing xfwl4. I don't vibe-code, ever, and I probably use the LLM to generate less code than most people do. After all, building things with code is my hobby and passion (and I'm lucky I got to do it professionally for a quarter century), and driving an LLM is kinda boring." We find this somewhat reassuring, but any really passionate anti-LLM Xfce users reading this may be glad that the release schedules of Ubuntu LTS versions and Xfce stable releases are so far out of sync – sticking with Xubuntu 26.04 means there's no immediate need to adopt the new LLM-assisted compositor. Or, of course, simply keep using X11 instead of Wayland – although that might eventually mean choosing a distro that maintains X11 support, perhaps through XLibre, which has other drawbacks for some. There are other options, too. We've also seen an independent fork of xfwm4 called xfwm4-gl . It's in active development and uses OpenGL to perform window compositing directly, while the current version uses the now rather old Xrender extension . Among the many organizations to adopt Outage As A Service (OAAS) were Microsoft , Apple , the FAA , and any number of European supermarkets . Even the NSA has succumbed. For us, at least, outage is word of the year. It's certainly deeply embedded in the public mind, with schoolchildren reportedly referring to the 19th century Irish famine as "the potato outage." There's no danger of an outrage outage. OAAS is synonymous with infrastructure failure, a more useful term that begins to hint at cause and cure as well as effect. In all of the latest crop, what we know is depressingly familiar. Microsoft's O365 meltdown was a cascading failure caused by a botched upgrade that took stuff offline and melted down as it tried to come back. The FAA was a migration from Jurassic hardware that wasn't end of life so much as living fossil. The Eurofridge-cum-fondue-maker was a control system so badly written it fell apart if you raised an eyebrow at it. Clearly, nobody had. Until now. These are all different classes of OAAS that have been around for decades. Security-based outages are still outages, and a packet flood is still a packet flood whether it's a botnet DDoS or finger trouble in the config dashboard. Each of them has a root cause with obvious fixes – a faulty mental model of network/server interaction, chronic underfunding, a complete supply chain with little cyber-security expertise. All these, like the poor, will be with us always. They won't fix themselves. Infrastructure that works is invisible, and invisible things are forgotten until they break. What's needed is an infrastructure that watches itself, that is designed to be adaptive and resilient, one that refuses to connect to danger and nulls out any that gets through. There have been attempts to create a ground-up architecture that is inherently risk resistant. One such is SCION (Scalability, Control, and Isolation On Next-generation networks). It redesigns routing between domains around explicit path selection, separate control and data planes, and mechanisms for trust and failure isolation. The result is a very resilient, very reliable, and very secure infrastructure that reflects the designers' tenet that you can't patch the internet into any of these things. Start from scratch or GTFO. SCION started about 15 years ago, and it works well enough to be adopted by entities like the Secure Swiss Finance Network . If the Gnomes of Zurich trust it, no higher accreditation exists. Well, it was designed by ETH Zürich. Where you won't find it is almost everywhere else. The internet is like Switzerland in the same way the Amazon rainforest is like Central Park. There are trees and sometimes it rains. It is unwise to infer anything else. technology.title: Software issues have even reached Mercury as BepiColombo probe arrives in uncertain state
technology.description: Humanity’s third-ever mission to Mercury has arrived, but a last-minute “software issue” has complicated matters. The BepiColombo mission is a joint effort by the European Space Agency (ESA) and Japan’s Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). Reaching Mercury is not easy because its gravity is weak and its orbit is fast. The tiny planet’s proximity to the Sun further complicates matters, because our star’s gravity accelerates everything that falls towards it. BepiColombo’s journey has therefore seen it whiz past Earth once, Venus twice, and Mercury six times on a complicated path the two space agencies designed to slow it down sufficiently to be captured by mercurial gravity, while also keeping up with its rapid orbit. In 2024, the craft’s thrusters underperformed, leading the ESA and JAXA to re-plot the planned trajectory and reschedule its arrival at Mercury from mid-2025 to this past weekend. The ESA’s operations team sent the commands to insert BepiColombo into orbit on Friday. On Sunday the craft phoned home with news that it entered orbit. A little later, however, the ESA revealed “the thruster burn was shorter than planned following a software issue.” The spacecraft is safe, but the ESA says it is “working to understand what happened” and promised updates early this week. Readers may recall that a pair of NASA missions to Mars are also experiencing software glitches , which have in recent weeks become all-too-prevalent on Earth, too. Fingers crossed If all is well, BepiColombo will deploy two orbiters. The ESA’s craft is called the Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO), which the ESA says will map the planet, assess the composition of its surface and interior, measure its magnetic field, and even gather data that scientists hope will “test Einstein's theory of General Relativity to an unprecedented level of accuracy.” JAXA’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MIO) will also investigate the planet’s magnetic field, plasma, dust, and atmosphere. Both orbiters are extraordinary feats of engineering. As JAXA explains , MIO is solar-powered but the sunlight it will receive at Mercury is around ten times as powerful as on Earth. Mercury itself is also sufficiently hot that the orbiter needs protection from heat radiated from the planet’s surface. ESA’s MPO keeps itself cool with three to four insulating blankets comprised of layered titanium, aluminum, and a ceramic fabric called Nextel. The blankets alone weigh 94kg. The two space agencies expect to start science operations in April 2027 but haven’t yet said if the two orbiters are in peak condition. JAXA, sadly, last week revealed that its Hayabusa2 probe has deteriorated to the point at which it can no longer make its planned landing on asteroid 1998 KY26. JAXA scheduled that for the year 2031, but problems with the probe’s thrusters mean the agency will instead attempt a high-speed fly-by of asteroid 2015 BM510 in 2028. technology.title: Techie turned his too-easy job interview into a trap
technology.description: Returning to work after the weekend can feel like voluntarily walking into a trap. To help readers feel a little freer, The Register therefore uses Monday mornings to serve up a new installment of " Who, Me? " It's the column in which we share your stories of mistakes, misjudgments, and occasional misanthropy. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Marshall," who told us about a job interview he endured about 20 years ago. The interview included a practical component he described as "Here's a PC, we've broken a few things in it, get it going." Marshall quickly spotted some mundane faults, such as a loose PCI card and unplugged internal cables. He felt the test was too easy. "One of the things I always checked was whether the power supply 110/230 switch was set for the UK," he told The Register . Getting the PC running earned Marshall a job offer, but he couldn't resist suggesting a tougher test. "I said to my future manager: 'Would it be a good thing to set the power supply to the wrong voltage as part of the interview test?' He said that wasn't fair." Marshall stayed in the job for two years. A couple of months after he left, his former manager sent him a short email. "Ha-ha, very funny." Marshall asked another former colleague what might have prompted that email. "It turned out somebody – I don't know if it was an interview candidate – had blown a power supply by not checking the voltage it was set to." What a coincidence! Or maybe not? "It wasn't anything to do with me," Marshall insisted. "No idea who it was." Have you held colleagues to a higher standard than the boss expected? Or left a little trap for them to trip over? In either case, click here to send email to Who, Me? We appreciate the chance to share your stories, and do so with appropriate anonymization so that contributors never step into the jaws of trouble. ®

technology.title: Google claims last week’s critical VMware bug was under attack in September
technology.description: Google’s Mandiant unit has claimed that the critical flaw VMware last week revealed in its vCenter product was under attack by a China-linked threat actor which knew of the bug in July and exploited it in September. VMware revealed several flaws on November 19. The big nasty is CVE-2026-123890, which allows unauthorized access to vCenter, the management console for hosts and guest VMs. According to seven researchers from Google’s threat intelligence group (formerly Mandiant), a crew it calls ARMORY CASTLE that it suspects of having links to the People’s Republic of China exploited CVE-2026-123890 by first compromising remote access appliances from BeyondTrust. Google’s analysis suggests the crew uses that toehold to establish access to other Linux appliances before moving deeper into victims’ networks. If the crew finds vCenter, it deploys a custom malware tool called “BONESAW” designed to slice into the VMware product. In the incident Google observed, BONESAW let attackers “forge authentication tokens, bypass MFA, and impersonate any user.” The gang put that access to work by conducting an inventory of the victim’s VMware setup, scooping up data describing the ESXi file system, attached disks, and mounted Virtual Machine File System volumes. ARMORY CASTLE also added an SSH public key to the root account’s authorized keys, and “conducted further reconnaissance and data theft on the ESXi filesystem using the root account.” Google also found evidence of BONESAW being used in July, on a server an unidentified entity had patched against CVE-2026-59309 – another authentication bypass vulnerability in vCenter. And BONESAW was just one of five tools Google thinks ARMORY CASTLE created as part of its plan to attack vCenter. It also made webshells named SLIMSAVAGE and CAGEMATCH, a backdoor called BEARBONES, and a SAML utility called SAWSNAKE. “The use of three separate specialized sets of malware and two zero-days in the course of a single campaign indicates that there are significant resources supporting ARMORY CASTLE operations,” Google’s researchers wrote. “It also shows the extent of the threat actor’s operational commitment to compromise high priority targets.” Few targets are as juicy as vCenter, because it can literally give attackers access to thousands of virtual machines and the hosts they run on. Google hasn't said how many attacks is saw on vCenter using BONESAW.
